title: what games do you actually want?
author: corbeezy
selftext: wondering for the public.... I've seen these podcasts about incremental games making a ton of money and I'm kind of into one I made... and I'm refining it... but also... I'd just love a great 3d platformer lol, but apparently that's a trap? and not something you should work on? I get the whole thing of just make what you like, but what do people actually want to play?

comments.author: bettertagsweretaken
comments.body: People want fun. Make the game engaging with a solid reward loop and the people who find it will stick around. How much of game design do you understand?

replies.author: corbeezy
replies.body: honestly like zero. i made a game like 5 years ago and gave up because i realized it was insanely terrible. i used to do standup comedy and spent years before i realized joke structure maybe i need to watch a basic game dev video to understand gameplay loops lol

replies.author: bettertagsweretaken
replies.body:
Then yes, definitely. Figure out how to manufacturer fun first, then iterate through different things you find fun and keep building until you have a system that makes you feel good when you run through it. 

Does it feel good, moment to moment? Why? How can you challenge that fun? What other elements can you introduce to put a spin on what's fun in your game? 

Games definitely aren't a thing you can jump into blind. You'll produce crap, but everyone has to start somewhere.

replies.author: loontoon
replies.body:
What an 8 year old finds fun and what a 50 year old finds fun are very different. 

What games a rich 8 year old plays will probably be pretty different to what an 8 year old from a poor family plays. 

There are too many variables to say what games people like.

replies.author: bettertagsweretaken
replies.body: Everything i said is still true. I didn't specify any age range. You have to target an audience, obviously? You can't produce anything coherent unless you have a coherent vision yourself. Like, duh? I didn't think i needed to say that part out loud. A lack of vision produces slop.

replies.author: loontoon
replies.body:
Yes, what you said is true, but I didn't think your comment went into enough detail.   
  
There is a tendency online for people to talk in broad terms without actually being very detailed. 

For example, people say AI games are slop.  Of course some are, but not all are.  Why can't people be less lazy and say which types of AI games are slop.  

I just wish people would be more specific in their writing.

comments.author: teamharder
comments.body: Im trying to find a balance between what's popular, what's realistic, and game genres I love/understand the feeling of. First game was a roguelike shoot em up (looks like Gladius). I'm straddling 3 games right now (open world RPG, kingdom builder, and horror FPS). Apparently horror does well, current idea is mechanically similar to one of my top 10 games (RE4), and I have asset packs to fill most of the holes. So Im going horror FPS (maybe roguelike as well since linking environents and narrative is currently a weakpoint of mine) and try pushing that to completion. Hopefully that resonates well with people.

comments.author: HighreachGrit
comments.body:
At this point for me any game that can be one shot by Claude isn't much of a game, and I wasn't a big fan of little flash type games before.

If you want to make what people like, you'll be making games like that though. For mobile. Huge market for simple, visually appealing games. Me, I like my games complicated so I like to make complicated games. I love a good game you can just live in for several hours at least. But I wouldn't say that's what the majority are looking for
